correctness.rationale: The lower bound is proved by an explicit finite product martingale and a prescribed-scale base-B realization. Direct conditioning gives martingale ratios tending to p/(p-1); arbitrary radius sets with unbounded logarithmic diameter contain the required finite separated chains; digit-position inequalities simultaneously freeze past coordinates and average future coordinates with quantified errors. Periodic localization and Lp-stable smoothing remove boundary and regularity issues. The upper bound follows from Madrid's exact unrestricted norm.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Madrid's abstract establishes the unrestricted exact norm, a detailed public review reports the dyadic-radii special case, and Wei--Nie--Wu--Yan prove equality for continuous upper truncations. Exact and synonymous literature searches and the current SCOPE archive did not locate the arbitrary irregular-radius theorem for every set with infimum zero or unbounded supremum, nor its finite-subfamily smooth-near-extremizer strengthening. The recent source paper was not available here in full text, so undisclosed broader coverage in that paper remains the main residual risk; dyadic radii are conservatively excluded from the originality claim.

value.rationale: The theorem shows that the newly determined sharp centered maximal constant is rigid under arbitrarily severe scale thinning: superlacunary and irregular radius sets retain the full constant whenever their logarithmic scale range is unbounded. The finite-subfamily strengthening isolates a reusable prescribed-scale martingale obstruction.
